newsitem.title: JAPAN: Daiei says sales down 10% since tax rise.
newsitem.headline: Daiei says sales down 10% since tax rise.

text.p: Sales at leading department store chain Daiei Inc are down 10 percent year-on-year since the sales tax was raised on April 1, Daiei executive vice president Jun Nakauchi said on Friday.
He said bad weather at the beginning of April may have also been a factor in the decline in sales.
Nakauchi said the company expects to post operating profits of 25 billion yen in 1997/98, which began on March 1, up from 2.5 billion yen in the previous year.
Daiei also expects sales at its existing stores to rise two percent in the current business year. In 1996/97, sales at existing stores fell 7.3 percent year-on-year.
It plans to open eight new stores this business year.
Referring to sluggish sales in 1996/97, Nakauchi said: "Our business was affected especially by the 0-157 food poisoning epidemic as well as sluggish sales of seasonal merchandise."
